title: Claude Code — proxy vs direct A/B
description: Controlled A/B of Claude Code through claude-switch-proxy vs direct to Anthropic: paired scripted sessions tagged by exp/scenario (services/cc-metrics/ab). Every panel splits by arm.

options.content:
**One experiment at a time.** Pick `exp` (an `ab_run.py` run id); every panel below is split by **arm** — **proxy** (blue, `claude` via claude-switch-proxy) vs **direct** (orange, `claude-direct` to api.anthropic.com). Sessions are scripted, **paired** (each replicate ran both arms with identical inputs, concurrently, in randomised order) and tagged by `scenario`. Filter `scenario` to a single one to compare like with like.

**Whole-experiment totals, not the time range.** An experiment's series exist only for that experiment, so every tile reads the counters' current values — exact totals since the run began, unaffected by the time picker (which only scopes the timeline row and *Turns per 10 min*). The main dashboard's range panels also work for an experiment, with Prometheus' `increase()` extrapolation on top.

**Read ratios, not counts.** The *direct ÷ proxy* row is the comparison: 1.00 = no difference. Metric definitions are the pre-registered ones in `services/cc-metrics/ab/CONTRACT.md` §5; `ab_report.py` computes the same numbers offline with paired bootstrap CIs — that report is the verdict, this page is the eyeball.

**Caveats.** Both arms share one Anthropic org, so one arm can warm the other's prompt cache (watch *cache hit ratio* on the first call). The proxy may route to a non-Anthropic lane; `model` is what Claude Code asked for, not what served it. Latency is estimated from transcript timestamps.
